I enjoy exploring ideas that combine software development, scientific data and real-world applications. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, I am independently working on an interactive Earth exploration experience that brings NASA data to life through 3D visualization, AI-powered insights and data sonification. I am eager to learn, experiment and create something meaningful.

EARTH — THE COMPLETE STORY is an interactive Earth exploration platform that combines NASA Earth observations, scientific visualizations and data-driven sonification to help people experience our changing planet through both sight and sound.
The project integrates NASA POWER for numerical environmental observations and NASA GIBS for satellite imagery. Users can explore historical and recent observations, investigate environmental variables such as temperature, precipitation, humidity and wind speed, and compare different time periods. Its Earth Jukebox uses the Web Audio API to dynamically translate actual NASA POWER observations into sound through documented mappings of scientific values to musical properties. Users can control playback and listen to how environmental conditions change over time.
By connecting Earth science data with sound, the project aims to make complex environmental information more engaging, understandable and accessible, including for people who may not rely entirely on visual representations. It transforms Earth observations into an interactive experience that users can both see and hear.
details:
Project Details — EARTH: THE COMPLETE STORY

EARTH — THE COMPLETE STORY is an interactive platform designed to help people explore and understand our changing planet through visualizations and sound. Inspired by NASA's Earth Information Jukebox challenge, the project aims to transform scientific Earth observations into an engaging audiovisual experience.

How does it work?

The platform integrates NASA POWER for numerical environmental observations and NASA GIBS for satellite imagery. Users can explore Earth through four modes: Past, Present, Changing and Future. They can investigate environmental variables such as temperature, precipitation, humidity and wind speed, explore observations across different dates, and compare two time periods to understand environmental changes.

The central feature is the Earth Jukebox, which uses the Web Audio API to convert actual NASA POWER numerical observations into sound. Different environmental variables influence sound characteristics through defined sonification mappings. This allows users to listen to patterns and changes in environmental data rather than relying exclusively on visual representations. Playback controls and audio visualizations help users interact with the generated sounds. Optional voice narration provides additional scientific explanations.

Benefits and intended impact

Environmental datasets can be complex and difficult for the general public to interpret. By combining scientific information with interactive visualizations and sonification, EARTH aims to make Earth science more engaging, approachable and accessible. It encourages users to explore environmental changes, understand scientific patterns and experience data through multiple senses. Sonification also offers an alternative way of engaging with information for people who may have difficulty accessing purely visual content.

Technologies used

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite and CSS.
  • 3D visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber and Drei.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Scientific data: NASA POWER and NASA GIBS.
  • Audio generation: Web Audio API and AnalyserNode.
  • Narration: Browser Speech Synthesis.

Creativity and design considerations

The project combines a cinematic, interactive 3D Earth experience with scientific data-driven sound. Instead of presenting environmental observations as conventional charts alone, it allows users to see and hear changes in the planet. Particular attention was given to scientific accuracy, genuine NASA observations, transparent sound mappings, missing-data handling, synchronized playback, accessibility, responsive design and user-controlled audio. The platform avoids fabricating observations or presenting unavailable future projections as established scientific results.

Ultimately, EARTH — THE COMPLETE STORY aims to make understanding our planet an immersive experience where Earth's data can be both seen and heard.
